title: New migration and asylum rules enter into application: what is changing?
date_evidence: Publication date 12 June 2026 (dateline '12 June 2026' on the Migration and Home Affairs news page; URL path .../2026-06-12_en)
key_claim: The EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, a package of 10 legislative acts, entered into application on 12 June 2026, introducing common screening, faster asylum and return procedures, a solidarity mechanism, and embedding migration in international partnerships including legal migration pathways.
frame_summary: The Commission frames the Pact as a comprehensive, strictly enforced system that pairs faster asylum and return procedures with international partnerships and legal-migration pathways.
notes: Tier-1 anchor for the Pact entering application on 12 June 2026. home-affairs.ec.europa.eu news page is largely server-rendered; the visible dateline reads 'Publication date 12 June 2026' and the URL slug encodes the date.

title: Commission welcomes political agreement on the Return Regulation
date_evidence: Publication date 2 June 2026 (dateline '2 June 2026' on the Migration and Home Affairs news page; URL path .../2026-06-02_en)
key_claim: The Return Regulation (political agreement reached 2 June 2026) makes readmission an integral part of the return process and facilitates data transfers with third countries; in parallel the Commission works with third countries to increase readmission cooperation using incentives such as readmission instruments, financing tools, visa and trade policy as part of the EU's migration diplomacy.
frame_summary: The Commission frames the Return Regulation as making returns faster and readmission integral, backed by cross-sector leverage (visa, trade and financial policy) over third countries.
verbatim_quote: such as readmission instruments, financing tools, visa and trade policy
notes: Tier-1 anchor for the leverage thesis. The home-affairs.ec.europa.eu page 403-bot-blocks the audit fetcher; manually verified via web_fetch on 2026-07-19: the on-page text reads 'This includes the use of incentives, such as readmission instruments, financing tools, visa and trade policy as part of the EU's migration diplomacy outreach to third countries.' Recorded verbatim_quote is an exact apostrophe-free substring, present on the page and quoted in the body.

title: Addressing worker shortages by attracting global talent
date_evidence: News article dateline '15 June 2026' under the title; footer 'Publication date 15 June 2026'
key_claim: The EU Talent Pool (the first EU-wide digital platform matching non-EU jobseekers with EU employers in shortage occupations) entered into force in June 2026, with the platform expected to be fully operational only by the end of 2027, alongside the updated Single Permit Directive; the Commission states legal migration complements its irregular-migration enforcement under the Pact.
frame_summary: The Commission frames the Talent Pool and Single Permit as the legal-migration complement to Pact enforcement within one 'balanced approach' to migration and asylum.
notes: Tier-1 source for the 'carrot' leg (Talent Pool + Single Permit) and the explicit framing that legal migration complements irregular-migration enforcement. Fetched clean; on-page line: 'They complement what the EU is doing to tackle irregular migration'.

title: EU Parliament backs EU Talent Pool to facilitate international recruitment for in-demand occupations
date_evidence: Publication Date: Tue 10 Mar 2026 (visible dateline at foot of article)
key_claim: On 11 March 2026 the European Parliament endorsed the EU Talent Pool by 414 votes to 182 with 21 abstentions; participation by Member States is voluntary, registration does not guarantee work or residence permits (which remain national), and trade-union bodies (ETF, EFFAT) warned the platform lacks dedicated worker-complaint mechanisms and safeguards, risking exploitation and social dumping.
frame_summary: EMN reports the Talent Pool as a voluntary, non-binding legal-migration tool endorsed by Parliament, while flagging trade-union concerns that its worker safeguards are insufficient.
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (10/03/2026, 3-6m band): canonical institutional record of the EP endorsement of the Talent Pool (on-page: '414 votes in favour, 182 against and 21 abstentions') and the trade-union safeguard critique used in the counter-argument. Only source outside the 3-month window; the single permitted anchor.

title: EU Talent Pool Regulation: New framework takes effect in June 2026
key_claim: The EU Talent Pool Regulation was published in the Official Journal on 12 May 2026 and applies from 1 June 2026; registration or selection confers no right of entry or residence, work and residence permits remain subject to national immigration law, Member-State participation is voluntary, and the platform is not necessarily operational from that date.
frame_summary: Ius Laboris advises employers that the Talent Pool is a recruitment-matching layer only: no right of entry, national permits still govern, and participation is voluntary.
notes: Tier-3 employer-facing law-firm-alliance analysis (Claeys & Engels for Ius Laboris), 22 May 2026. Supplies the 'thin carrot' evidence (on-page: 'does not confer any right of entry or residence. Work and residence permits remain subject to national immigration law'), plus the OJ/application dates.

title: Guinea refuses to readmit irregular migrants; the EU suspends visas
key_claim: On 10 July 2026 the Council of the EU decided to temporarily restrict Schengen visa provision for Guinean nationals under Article 25a of the Visa Code, after a Commission assessment found Guinea's cooperation on readmitting its nationals insufficient: all 27 Member States will stop issuing multiple-entry visas and documentation-requirement exemptions to Guineans, diplomatic/service passport fee waivers are suspended, and standard visa processing rises to 45 calendar days from 15.
frame_summary: Eunews frames the Guinea visa suspension as the EU adopting a retaliatory 'no readmission, no visas' leverage posture as a new default.
notes: Tier-3 quality journalism (Eunews/Withub), 10 July 2026, reporting the Council's Article 25a visa measure on Guinea, the concrete leverage instance running alongside the Talent Pool 'carrot'. On-page: 'the standard processing time for visa applications will be set at 45 calendar days, instead of 15'; Council quote 'temporarily restrict visa provision for Guinean nationals'.

title: Questions and Answers: The EU Pact on Migration and Asylum
key_claim: Human Rights Watch argues the Pact expands externalisation and 'safe third country' arrangements, allows deportation before appeals are decided on the merits, and warns that tying cooperation to leverage over third countries risks rights violations; it calls on Member States to refrain from safe-third-country agreements and to take responsibility for examining asylum claims.
frame_summary: HRW argues the Pact entrenches externalisation and erodes asylum safeguards, warning that leveraging third countries for returns risks rights violations without ensuring protection.
notes: Tier-4 advocacy source used directionally for the counter-argument (rights and effectiveness critique of the Pact's externalisation/third-country approach). Published 10 June 2026.
